# @zakkster/lite-lru

Zero-dependency, zero-GC cache FAMILY for JavaScript under one uniform
LiteCache<K,V> surface. A classic LRU reference member (LiteLru), the modern SIEVE
headline (Sieve), the admission-controlled S3-FIFO member (S3Fifo), the
frequency-admission W-TinyLFU member (WTinyLfu), the two scan-resistant
baselines Segmented-LRU (Slru) and 2Q (TwoQ), the no-tuning adaptive member
ARC (Arc), the scan/loop-resistant recency-of-recency member LIRS (Lirs), the
O(1) EXACT least-frequently-used member (Lfu), the CLOCK-approximation-of-LIRS
member CLOCK-Pro (ClockPro), the classic recency-of-recency member LRU-K
(K=2) (LruK), the frequency-band-with-logical-decay member Multi-Queue
(m=8) (Mq), and the CLOCK-reformulation-of-ARC member CAR (Car)
expose the
SAME get/put/has/peek/delete/clear API, so the eviction policy is a one-line
constructor swap. Single-file ESM, zero runtime
dependencies, node:test only. Ships a runnable + importable benchmark tool
(Bench.mjs) with Belady OPT so a caller measures which policy fits their trace
instead of guessing.

## Status: 1.19.0 - H1 hardening (ROADMAP S17): TTL put and the default clock no longer allocate (expiry validated and computed at the top of put into a per-instance Float64Array(1); default clock is now performance.timeOrigin + performance.now(), epoch-anchored and monotonic -- inject Date.now for wall time; a 1.18.0 snapshot restores with the same remaining TTLs); W-TinyLFU sketch hash folded into Smi range; restore() rejects duplicate keys and non-number/NaN/null expiries; DirectLru rejects unknown options; a NaN clock reads stale and throws on put before any mutation; capacity > 2^31-1 rejected; clear() is O(size); new getters keysBacking / maxKey / ttlEnabled / statsEnabled; TTL-on zero-alloc lanes (0 scavenges at N and 8N, all 13 members). Test count 1918 -> 2359. Built atop 1.18.0 (benchmark-only, no Lru.js change: benchmark/Bench.mjs gains skew + variance axes -- an alphas zipf-exponent sweep (exported ZIPF_ALPHAS = [0.7,0.9,1.0,1.2], naming zipf-a<A>), a keyspaceRatio knob (default 16, was hardcoded), per-member nsPerOpMedian + nsPerOpP95 over a repeats-pass timing loop (default 5; no single-throughput headline), a seeded webTrace diurnal-hot-set generator, and a parseIntTrace(text) columnar loader; the new knobs live in a top-level tuning object and the default runBench() output is byte-unchanged (config stays {capacity,length,seed}). beladyOpt's Int32Array(n)+Map scale ceiling is documented (OPT, not the caches, caps a scale run). Built atop 1.17.0 (adds a THIRD keyed-index backing, keys:'dense' (decisions/0029), plus a thin DirectLru wrapper). The dense backing is a DIRECT-MAPPED, generation-stamped typed-array index for a SMALL, DENSE integer key domain [0, maxKey]: the hot body is a single array read `_gen[k] === _epoch ? _ixSlot[k] : NIL` -- NO hash, NO probe, NO per-op init. STRICT zero-alloc (measured 0.00000 B/op on get/put/delete/has/peek), and clear() is genuinely O(1) via an epoch bump (only a disclosed-amortized O(U) reset when the epoch would overflow INT_MAX). The no-init trick borrows the sparse-set discipline: `_gen` is a zero-initialized Int32Array and `_epoch` starts at 1, so a never-written key reads absent with no O(U) pre-fill and 0 is a LEGAL key. The honest co-headline is SPACE: O(maxKey), NOT O(entries) -- two [0, maxKey] Int32Arrays. Bench (same LRU policy, integer dense-domain zipf, capacity 256): keys:'dense' ~40 ns/op vs keys:'int' ~50 vs the default Map ~64, identical hit ratio (a substrate swap, not a policy change). DirectLru(cap, { maxKey }) is byte-identical to new LiteLru(cap, { keys:'dense', maxKey }) -- ZERO policy duplication, every hot path + dump/restore inherited. snapBase now reads an explicit _store._kind tag ('map'|'int'|'dense') instead of duck-typing on checkStable (which the dense store also has), so a dense cache dumps as keys:'dense'+mk(maxKey) and restores exactly. All 13 members thread maxKey and can ride the dense backing; the default Map + keys:'int' paths are byte-unchanged. Test count 1754 -> 1886. Built atop 1.16.1 (completes the v1.16.0 shape-hygiene pass and locks its fail-closed doors with a boundary suite). ClockPro + Lirs now initialize the onEvict fire-after fields (_evKey/_evVal) at construction, matching Car/LruK/Mq, so no member's object shape transitions on first eviction (all five now identical; test-verified, torture-clean). A new 287-case cross-member boundary suite (test/Options.test.js) locks the v1.16.0 doors -- unknown-key did-you-mean hints, non-object bag rejection, non-function onEvict rejection, and the Symbol/BigInt options footgun -- across all thirteen members, plus a beladyOpt Infinity case; test count 1466 -> 1754. Built atop 1.16.0 (fail-closed doors + measurement correctness across the complete thirteen-member family: every constructor rejects an unknown option key with a did-you-mean hint and a non-function onEvict at the door; the bench/harness PRNG is a true full-period xorshift32, logical >>> 17 -- seeded traces changed, bench table regenerated; every torture tier returns a positive work-unit count or the gate fails; beladyOpt rejects non-numeric capacity) and Car (1.15.0: the THIRTEENTH member (Bansal & Modha, "CAR: Clock with Adaptive Replacement", USENIX FAST'04): the CLOCK reformulation of ARC, completing the CLOCK-approximation trio -- ClockPro is to LIRS what Car is to ARC (as Lfu/WTinyLfu are the exact/approximate frequency pair). Patent-cleared before any code (the direct CAR/CART filing US 2006/0069876 A1, Bansal & Modha/IBM, was ABANDONED and never granted; the adjacent temporal-filtering patents US 7,058,766 + US 7,096,321 expired 2024; ARC's US 6,996,676 expired 2024-02-22) -- due diligence, NOT legal advice; US filings only. Two reference-bit CLOCK lists T1 (recency) and T2 (frequency) ride the shared _next/_prev columns, each walked by a hand (_hT1/_hT2); a per-slot _st byte carries bit0 reference + bit1 inT2. Two keys-only bounded ghosts B1 (cap capacity) and B2 (cap 2*capacity) via CarHistory extends ArcGhost, plus an adaptive integer target p for |T1| that a B1 hit raises (toward recency) and a B2 hit lowers -- ARC's self-tuning split, no knobs. HOT PATH: a hit sets ONE reference bit (_st |= CAR_REF) -- 0 link writes, exactly 1 _st store, and NEVER calls _replace (the Sieve/ClockPro 0-link-write headline; CAR never promotes on hit, so there is no hidden relink to hide). EVICTION: _replace rotates the T1/T2 hands, migrating a referenced page to T2 and clearing its bit, and evicts the first page it finds with reference bit 0. HONEST BOUND (reviewer + qa enforced, deliberately NOT the ClockPro S18 overclaim): eviction is amortized O(1) per miss but WORST-CASE O(capacity) reference-bit clears + link writes on a full-scan-then-insert -- there is NO pinned constant miss+evict bound (the t6 carStream worst-observed=109, tripwire=288, is a per-stream regression TRIPWIRE, not a cap), UNLIKE Lfu's proven <=14 or Mq's proven <=33. Directory invariants: |T1|+|T2|==size<=capacity, |T1|+|B1|<=capacity, total<=2*capacity, a key in EXACTLY ONE of T1/T2/B1/B2; resident value capacity stays EXACTLY capacity. Gate CAR strict zero-alloc (keys:'int', 0.00000 B/op, writes/hit links=0 state=1), maxPauseMs 0.000. new LiteLru(n) <-> ... <-> new Mq(n) <-> new Car(n), type-checked; TTL / iteration (T2 MRU..LRU then T1, ghost-excluded, recency-neutral, fail-closed mid-walk) / stats / snapshot (both clocks + per-slot ref bits + T1/T2 membership + B1/B2 ghosts + adaptive p + both hand positions verbatim, tag m:'Car', fail-closed restore) / bench / the demo all extend to the thirteenth member. The roster is now THIRTEEN members and the family is declared COMPLETE at thirteen (CART deferred: its T1-vs-T2 entry rule is a tuning delta, not a distinct mental model). The repo-only GUIDE.md (decision table + mermaid flowchart + a per-member mental model of all thirteen + measured seeded-bench numbers, whose GOLDEN RULE is to MEASURE your own trace with runBench + beladyOpt rather than choose by theory, documenting the honest finding that ClockPro scores 0% of Belady OPT on a pure loop where Lirs hits 99.2% and WTinyLfu 94.4%) gains its Car row. The lite-perf-gate dev-only zero-alloc node:test gate (`npm run test:perf` in `verify`) extends to 26 int-backed scenarios (all thirteen members x get-hit + put-churn). Built atop Mq (1.14.0: the Multi-Queue second-level / server buffer-cache member with logical-time frequency decay), LruK (1.13.0: the original LRU-K recency-of-recency member), ClockPro (1.12.0: the CLOCK approximation of LIRS + the lite-perf-gate integration), LFU (1.11.0: the O(1) exact least-frequently-used member), LIRS (1.10.0: recency-of-recency, bounded non-resident history, loop 99.2% of Belady OPT), the policy-visualization demo (a never-shipped demo/ that animates all thirteen members on one trace drawn strictly from dump(), served by a zero-dep Node demo/serve.mjs, fails closed off-server), snapshot / restore (1.8.0: a COLD dump() + static restore(snap, opts?), the SoA columns ARE the serial form, no substrate field / no hot-path branch, EXACT future-eviction round-trip, fail-closed restore tag {f,m,cap,keys,ttl,t}, TTL absolute-not-rebased), the no-tuning adaptive member Arc (1.7.0), the scan-resistant baselines Slru/TwoQ (1.6.0), opt-in zero-GC stats (1.5.0), zero-GC iteration (1.4.0), opt-in zero-GC TTL (1.3.0), and the shipped bench + Belady OPT tool.)

The family is the identity from v1.0.0: classic LRU is the reference member +
differential oracle + honest floor, SIEVE is the headline, and the shipped
measurement tool is the differentiator neither lru-cache nor quick-lru offers.

S0 landed the classic core (Map + intrusive preallocated doubly-linked list;
get/put/delete/has/peek/clear; onEvict; fail-closed capacity). S1 built the
node:test suite + the policy-parameterized differential oracle + torture harness,
and found + fixed the onEvict reentrancy defect (fire-after ordering + a
fail-closed guard, decisions/0002). S3 factored the shared keyed-index substrate
(SlotStore) and added the opt-in keys:'int' open-addressed typed-array index for
STRICT zero-alloc (decisions/0011). S4 added SIEVE as the first modern member on
that substrate (decisions/0012). S9 (this session) adds the docs, the shipped
bench + Belady OPT tool, and the OPT torture gate -- with ZERO change to Lru.js /
Lru.d.ts (the three version sites move together, only at /release).

## Members (decisions/0001, 0012, 0013, 0014, 0015, 0016, 0023, 0024, 0025, 0026, 0027, 0028)

All classes implement LiteCache<K,V>; the recency/lazy-promotion/admission/adaptive/
frequency difference is INTERNAL, so new LiteLru(n) swaps for new Sieve(n), new S3Fifo(n),
new WTinyLfu(n), new Slru(n), new TwoQ(n), new Arc(n), new Lirs(n), new Lfu(n),
new ClockPro(n), new LruK(n), new Mq(n) or new Car(n) and stays
type-checked. For which member to pick per workload (a decision flowchart + measured
bench numbers + a per-member mental model), see GUIDE.md in the repo (repo-only, not in
the npm tarball); the golden rule is to MEASURE your own trace with runBench + beladyOpt
rather than choose by theory.

- LiteLru: classic Least-Recently-Used. get/put promote to most-recently-used;
  at capacity a new key evicts the LRU tail and reuses its slot in place. A hit
  on the MRU head early-returns (0 writes); an interior/tail hit relinks a small
  constant (5 / 4 index stores, pinned by the torture gate). The reference member
  + the differential oracle + the honest floor.
- Sieve: SIEVE (Zhang et al., NSDI'24). A lazy-promotion FIFO ring with ONE
  visited byte per entry and ONE moving hand. A hit sets the visited byte and
  does NOTHING structural (0 link writes, exactly 1 visited-byte store -- the
  headline). At capacity the hand sweeps FIFO order, grants each visited entry a
  single second chance, and evicts the first unvisited entry in place. has/peek
  are visited-neutral. Scan-resistant where LRU is not.
- S3Fifo: S3-FIFO (Yang et al., SOSP'23). Quick-demotion + lazy-promotion over a
  SMALL probation FIFO (~10% of capacity), a MAIN FIFO, and a bounded keys-only
  GHOST queue. A hit sets the visited byte and does NOTHING structural (same 0
  link writes, 1 visited-byte store as SIEVE). Newcomers enter SMALL unvisited,
  unless the key is in ghost (a second sighting) -> straight to MAIN. At capacity
  one eviction step: the SMALL oldest graduates to MAIN if proven (visited), else
  is evicted and its key remembered in ghost; otherwise the MAIN oldest gets one
  second chance or is evicted (MAIN evictions are NOT ghosted). has/peek are
  visited-neutral; the ghost holds KEYS only, never values. Strongly scan-resistant.
- WTinyLfu: W-TinyLFU (Einziger et al., "TinyLFU"; the Caffeine approach). A small
  admission WINDOW (an LRU, ~1% of capacity) in front of a segmented main cache
  (SLRU: a PROBATION segment + a PROTECTED segment), all three lists threaded
  through the shared _next/_prev columns (tagged per slot by _seg), gated by a
  fixed Count-Min sketch (4 rows of 4-bit saturating counters packed 8-per-Uint32,
  width pow2 >= capacity, aged by halving every counter in place every 10*capacity
  bumps). get/put bump the sketch and promote within the segment (a probation hit
  is PROMOTED to protected). At capacity the window's LRU is the admission
  CANDIDATE, weighed against the probation LRU VICTIM: admit the candidate (evict
  the victim) iff freq(cand) > freq(victim); ties reject (favor the incumbent). A
  hit does MORE work than SIEVE/S3-FIFO (a segment relink + a 4-counter bump) BY
  DESIGN -- still zero allocation. Scan- AND frequency-resistant; the best fit for
  skewed (Zipf) traffic, often closest to Belady OPT. Sizing: window =
  max(1,round(cap/100)); main = cap-window; protected = round(main*0.8); the
  degenerate main==0 edge (capacity 1) is a window-only LRU. Sketch hashing: number/
  string keys hash by VALUE; object keys hash by RESIDENT SLOT (no WeakMap, bumped
  only while resident -- decisions/0014). has/peek are frequency- and recency-neutral.
- Slru: Segmented LRU (decisions/0015). A probation FIFO (~20%) in front of a
  protected LRU (protectedCap = round(capacity*0.8)), two lists threaded through the
  shared _next/_prev columns (tagged per slot by _seg). A newcomer enters probation;
  the promote-on-2nd-hit law holds -- get(X) once leaves X in probation (a visited bit
  set, no reorder), get(X) twice promotes X to protected (put(update) counts as a hit);
  a promotion that overflows protected demotes its LRU tail back to probation. A
  protected hit moves to protected MRU. Eviction ALWAYS prefers the probation tail, so
  a cap-sized distinct-key scan evicts 0 protected entries -- the simplest
  scan-resistant baseline. has/peek are promotion-neutral.
- TwoQ: the full 2Q (Johnson & Shasha, VLDB'94), decisions/0015. An A1in FIFO
  (a1inCap = max(1,round(capacity*0.25))) + an Am LRU + a fixed, keys-only A1out ghost
  (ghostCap = capacity-a1inCap) reusing the S3-FIFO ghost-ring pattern (strict
  zero-alloc on keys:'int', amortized on the default Map backing). A newcomer enters
  A1in unless the key is in the A1out ghost (a second sighting) -> straight to Am,
  consumed from the ghost (the ONLY path into Am). An A1in hit does NOTHING (pure FIFO
  probation -- no promotion); an Am hit moves to Am MRU. At capacity the reclaim step
  evicts the A1in tail (recording its key in the ghost) when A1in is over its target or
  Am is empty, else the Am LRU (not ghosted). A distinct one-hit-wonder flood churns
  A1in only, never displacing Am. has/peek are neutral; the ghost holds KEYS only.
- Arc: the Adaptive Replacement Cache (Megiddo & Modha, FAST'03; patent expired),
  decisions/0016. A RECENT list T1 (seen once) + a FREQUENT list T2 (seen 2+) threaded
  through the shared _next/_prev columns (tagged per slot by _seg = 0/1), plus two
  bounded keys-only ghosts B1/B2 (the S3-FIFO/TwoQ ring pattern, factored into an
  internal ArcGhost; strict zero-alloc on keys:'int', amortized on the Map backing). A
  single integer p (the T1 target, 0..capacity) self-tunes the split -- no knobs. A hit
  (get or put-update) promotes to T2 (frequent). A new put whose key is in B1 raises p
  (p += max(1, floor(|B2|/|B1|)), capped at capacity) and re-admits to T2; in B2 lowers p
  (p -= max(1, floor(|B1|/|B2|)), floored at 0) and re-admits to T2. At capacity REPLACE
  evicts the T1 LRU (to B1) when |T1| > p or the boundary key-in-B2 && |T1| == p, else
  the T2 LRU (to B2); the all-recent |T1| == c edge direct-evicts the T1 LRU with no
  ghost. RESIDENT value capacity stays EXACTLY capacity -- only the split adapts, never
  the total (D16.2); bounds |T1|+|B1| <= c and |B1|+|B2| <= c hold. has/peek are neutral;
  a get never touches the ghosts.
- Lirs: LIRS (Jiang & Zhang, SIGMETRICS'02), decisions/0023. Eviction by
  RECENCY-OF-RECENCY: a block's IRR (inter-reference recency) is the count of DISTINCT
  blocks referenced between its last two accesses. Low-IRR blocks are the hot LIR set
  (resident); high-IRR blocks are HIR (a small resident reserve + non-resident metadata).
  Structure: a LIR set + a list Q of resident-HIR eviction candidates (both threaded
  through the shared _next/_prev columns, a disjoint resident partition), an interleaved
  stack S on its own member columns (per-slot _st byte: bit0 LIR, bit1 inS), and a BOUNDED
  non-resident history -- LirsHistory extends ArcGhost, keys-only, cap = capacity,
  drop-OLDEST (strict zero-alloc on keys:'int', amortized on the Map backing). Split:
  L_hir = max(1, round(capacity*0.01)) resident-HIR slots, L_lir = capacity - L_hir LIR
  slots; RESIDENT value capacity stays EXACTLY capacity (only the split moves,
  |LIR|+|resident HIR| == size). A LIR hit moves to the top of S (0 link writes at the top,
  else the 5-write move); a resident-HIR hit while IN S reclassifies to LIR (demoting the
  bottom LIR to Q, then pruning); a returning key still in the bounded history is re-admitted
  as LIR (the loop/scan discriminator). At capacity the Q front (LRU resident HIR) is
  evicted. has/peek are neutral. D23 BOUNDED LIRS VARIANT (honest, NOT textbook-exact): the
  non-resident history is a SEPARATE bounded FIFO ring rather than entries interleaved in
  the stack, so "still in S" is eviction-recency membership (FIFO) rather than textbook
  stack-position, and a single access's STACK PRUNING is O(L_hir) (measured max 41 at
  cap 4096, worst-case op ~0.02 ms) rather than textbook O(capacity) -- a strict latency
  improvement, measured + pinned, never capped. Best loop/scan resistance in the family:
  on a loop LARGER than capacity it keeps the LIR set stable where LRU thrashes (bench loop
  99.2% of Belady OPT vs ~0% for the other members; scan 100% of OPT).
- Lfu: O(1) EXACT Least-Frequently-Used (Shah-Matani), decisions/0024. A doubly-linked
  list OF frequency BUCKETS in ascending order (_bMin = head = lowest freq = eviction end);
  each bucket owns a recency list of the resident keys at ONE exact frequency, threaded
  through the MEMBER columns _fNext/_fPrev (NOT the shared _next/_prev; _kB tags the owning
  bucket). Frequency lives ON the bucket in a Float64Array _bFreq (EXACT to 2^53, no 2^31
  wrap - same rationale as stats D19.4), NOT an Int32Array. The bucket POOL is preallocated
  to capacity (at most capacity distinct frequencies among <= capacity keys - provably
  enough), drawn from a _bFree stack, NEVER new per bucket; exhaustion fails CLOSED. A hit
  (get or put-UPDATE, D24) increments the key's frequency by one and relinks it to the MRU
  end of the freq+1 bucket - zero-ALLOCATION but NOT zero-write (a bucket relink, pinned <= 14
  index stores/hit; a single-key bucket with no freq+1 neighbour is RELABELLED in place at 1
  write, the fast path). WITHIN-BUCKET TIE-BREAK = LRU: newcomer + just-promoted attach at MRU,
  eviction takes the LRU-end key of the lowest-frequency bucket. has/peek are frequency-neutral.
  This is EXACT frequency counting - the counterpart to WTinyLfu's APPROXIMATE count-min sketch:
  reach for Lfu when you need a PROVABLE "least-frequently-used is the victim" (audits, quota
  fairness, deterministic replay), not a statistical estimate. O(1) get/put/increment/evict -
  NOT the O(log n) of a heap-based LFU. Ascending-frequency iteration (MRU..LRU per bucket);
  snapshot captures EXACT per-bucket frequencies verbatim (dropping them is a fail-OPEN
  future-eviction bug - the t9 lfu-freq-dropped control catches it; lfu-approx-freq proves a
  saturating counter diverges from the exact oracle).
- ClockPro: CLOCK-Pro (Jiang, Chen & Zhang, USENIX ATC'05), decisions/0025. The CLOCK
  approximation of LIRS: recency-of-recency on ONE circular clock of resident pages + per-page
  state bits (_st: bit0 hot, bit1 referenced, bit2 test) + THREE Int32 hands (_handCold
  eviction, _handHot demotion, _handTest test-period expiry). A hit sets the reference bit ONLY
  - 0 link writes, exactly 1 _st store (the Sieve/S3Fifo lazy-promotion headline; put-update
  also sets ref, has/peek are reference-neutral). The clock is realized as a NIL-terminated DLL
  (_head newest .. _tail oldest) with wrap-around hand advance (_advance(_tail)->_head), so the
  traversal is circular but iteration/conservation/snapshot reuse the shared machinery
  byte-for-byte (the one documented D25 deviation). ADAPTIVE integer hot target _mHot (0..cap):
  a re-admit of a key still in the bounded non-resident history RAISES it (page proved worthy,
  re-admitted HOT); HAND_test ending a test period unreferenced LOWERS it - O(1) both. RESIDENT
  capacity is EXACTLY capacity; only the hot/cold split moves (_nHot+_nCold==size). Bounded
  non-resident test-page history (ClockProHistory extends ArcGhost, keys-only, cap = capacity,
  drop-oldest, NOT interleaved into the clock - the honest bounded deviation, mirrors Lirs).
  Exact/approximate pair with Lirs the way Lfu/WTinyLfu are for frequency. Gate CLOCKPRO strict
  zero-alloc (keys:'int'), writes/hit 0 links + 1 state (a REAL pin); eviction amortized O(1) per
  miss (classic CLOCK) but WORST-CASE O(capacity) writes on a full-scan-then-insert (reference every
  resident page, then insert -> the sweep clears every reference bit) - NOT a constant, so the t6
  miss+evict worst-observed is a per-stream (cpStream) regression TRIPWIRE, not a bound; snapshot
  captures the clock + all three hands + _mHot + test bits + history verbatim (dropping any is fail-OPEN -
  t9 clockpro-hands-dropped / clockpro-mhot-dropped / clockpro-test-bits-dropped catch it;
  clockpro-no-adapt proves freezing _mHot diverges).
- LruK: LRU-K (O'Neil, O'Neil & Weikum, SIGMOD'93), K=2, decisions/0026. The original
  recency-of-recency policy: evicts by the K-th BACKWARD DISTANCE (the time of a page's
  K-th-most-recent reference). Fixed K=2 (LRU-2), no knob and no correlated-reference period
  (CRP). A page is COLD until its 2nd reference, then WARM; two Float64 columns _r0 (most-recent
  reference time) + _r1 (2nd-most-recent = the K=2 backward distance) are allocated WITH the
  store (never per-key). HOT PATH: a warm hit slides _r1=_r0 then stamps _r0=++_t - 0 link writes,
  exactly 2 stamps; a cold->warm promotion unlinks the cold list + pushes the warm list - at most
  5 (2..5) link writes, non-exceedable (up to 2 cold-detach + up to 3 warm-push; 5 is the reachable
  maximum, pinned by CountedLruK) + the same 2 stamps. A cold page's _r1 sits at the -Infinity SENTINEL (D26.3: null is not zero - a cold
  page is K-distance INFINITE, evicted first). Two disjoint lists over the shared _next/_prev
  columns (COLD _coldHead..coldTail, WARM _warmHead..warmTail). EVICTION: the cold tail first
  (O(1) - infinite K-distance goes first); only when NO cold page exists, a LINEAR min-_r1 scan
  over the warm list - honestly O(size) READS, O(1) writes, NOT amortized O(1) and NO claimed
  bound (t6 measures the all-warm worst-observed scan length as a per-stream regression TRIPWIRE,
  never a cap; the true worst case is O(capacity)). Bounded keys-only non-resident history
  (LruKHistory extends ArcGhost, cap = capacity, drop-oldest); a put of a key still in it re-admits
  the page WARM at _r1=_r0=++_t (the bounded, keys-only deviation from the paper's timestamped
  HIST(p), documented D26.4). RESIDENT capacity is EXACTLY capacity (|cold|+|warm|==size). vs LRU:
  put X,Y,Z; get Y,Z,X -> the next insert evicts X (min-r1), where classic LRU evicts Y. Gate LRUK
  strict zero-alloc (keys:'int'), writes/hit 0 links + 2 stamps (warm) / at most 5 (2..5) links,
  non-exceedable, + 2 stamps (promote); snapshot captures both lists + the r0/r1 columns + the
  logical clock + the history verbatim (dropping any is fail-OPEN - t9 lruk-drop-r1 /
  lruk-lru-tiebreak catch it). DOCUMENTED LIMITATION, not a bug: a snapshot with COLD pages is
  NOT plain-JSON round-trippable -- the cold _r1 sentinel (-Infinity) degrades to null under
  JSON.stringify, so restore() fails CLOSED with a numeric-column error; structuredClone
  round-trips fine.
- Mq: Multi-Queue (Zhou, Philbin & Li, USENIX ATC'01), m=8, decisions/0027. Rank by FREQUENCY
  BAND with LOGICAL-time decay. Each block carries a reference count; its band is
  band(rc)=min(floor(log2(rc)),7) - the highest set bit of rc, CLAMPED (D27.3: rc>=128 saturates
  to Q7 so Math.clz32, which coerces mod 2^32, never wraps _qn/_qHead/_qTail out of range - a
  FAIL-CLOSED guard, not an optimization). 8 LRU queues Q0..Q7 ride the shared _next/_prev columns
  (_qHead/_qTail Int32Array(8), _qn Uint8 band per slot). HOT PATH (honest, D27.6): a hit bumps rc,
  re-bands, and MOVES the block to the MRU of its band - 0 link writes when already the band MRU,
  else AT MOST 5 (4..5: <=2 detach + <=3 head push) - then stamps _exq=_t+lifeTime (lifeTime=capacity, on
  a LOGICAL clock _t SEPARATE from the wall-clock ttl, D27.2), then runs a FIXED m-1=7-step aging
  sweep: for each band Q1..Q7 demote its idle tail one level toward Q0 (<=4 links each). This is NOT
  a 0-write lazy-promotion hit (unlike Sieve/ClockPro/LruK-warm) - said plainly. The per-access cost
  is a PROVEN non-exceedable <=33 link writes (5 relink + 7x4 aging) + 3 metadata stamps (_rc,_qn,
  _exq): reset-on-demote FORBIDS CASCADE (a demoted block lands at the HEAD of an already-visited
  lower band with a fresh _exq, never re-examined this sweep), so it is a REAL constant (like Lfu's
  proven 14), pinned + measured by CountedMq (worst-observed 17 links, 3 demotions/sweep, never >7).
  EVICTION: the LRU tail of the LOWEST non-empty queue (O(1), D27.4) - a decayed once-hot block in
  Q0 goes before a still-hot high-band one. Bounded keys-only + REFCOUNT Qout (MqHistory extends
  ArcGhost + a parallel Float64 refcount ring, cap=capacity, drop-oldest, D27.5); a put of a key
  still in Qout re-admits it at rc=savedRc+1 (an evicted rc-5 block re-enters at band(6)=Q2). vs
  Lfu: Mq FORGETS via logical decay where Lfu never does. Gate MQ strict zero-alloc (keys:'int',
  0.00000 B/op), maxPauseMs 0.000; snapshot captures the 8 queues + the rc/exq columns + the logical
  clock + the Qout keys+refcounts verbatim, tag m:'Mq', fail-closed restore (dropping any is
  fail-OPEN - t9 mq-no-aging / mq-drop-rc catch it).
- Car: CAR, Clock with Adaptive Replacement (Bansal & Modha, USENIX FAST'04), decisions/0028.
  The CLOCK REFORMULATION of ARC - ARC's exact semantics (two lists T1 recent / T2 frequent,
  keys-only ghosts B1/B2, one adaptive integer p in [0,c], no knobs) realized on reference-bit
  CLOCKS instead of ARC's LRU lists, so a HIT sets ONE reference bit and MOVES NOTHING (the
  Sieve/S3-FIFO/ClockPro 0-link-write hit, D28.5) where ARC relinks to the T2 MRU. Completes the
  CLOCK-approximation trio (SIEVE / ClockPro / CAR); sibling to ClockPro (the CLOCK approximation
  of LIRS). Two circular clocks ride the shared _next/_prev columns (NIL-terminated DLLs with
  wrap-around hands _hT1/_hT2; _st bit0 = reference, bit1 = inT2). HOT PATH: get / put-update do
  exactly _st[s] |= CAR_REF -- 0 link writes, exactly 1 _st store (pinned + measured by CountedCar
  PER CALL SITE). COLD PATH _replace() (D28.4): from the T1 hand when |T1| >= max(1,p) else the T2
  hand, a REFERENCED page has its ref bit CLEARED and MIGRATES to the T2 MRU (a T1 survivor) or
  rotates within T2 (a T2 survivor); the first UNREFERENCED page found is the victim -> B1 (from T1)
  or B2 (from T2). A B1 (recent) ghost hit RAISES p, a B2 (frequent) ghost hit LOWERS it; a ghost
  re-admit re-enters T2. Fixed-capacity honesty (D28.4): resident value cap is EXACTLY capacity,
  only the T1/T2 split adapts; bounded ghosts |T1|+|B1| <= c and directory total |T1|+|T2|+|B1|+|B2|
  <= 2c. HONEST COST (D28.6, the recurring ClockPro cautionary tale): the HIT is a genuine
  0-link-write / 1-_st-store; the miss+EVICT is AMORTIZED O(1) (classic CLOCK) but WORST-CASE
  O(capacity) reference-bit clears on a full-scan-then-insert -- NO pinned constant bound (unlike
  Lfu's proven 14 or Mq's proven 33); the torture carStream worst-observed is a per-stream
  regression TRIPWIRE, not a cap. The ref-bit CLEARS live entirely on the miss/evict path in
  _replace, never the hit budget (CountedCar attributes them per call site). Gate CAR strict
  zero-alloc (keys:'int', 0.00000 B/op), maxPauseMs 0.000; snapshot captures the T2/T1 clocks +
  each page's _st byte + the two hands + p + both ghosts verbatim, tag m:'Car', fail-closed restore
  (dropping any is fail-OPEN - t9 car-no-adapt / car-p-dropped / car-ref-bits-dropped catch it). vs
  Arc: CAR is ARC on clocks (a 0-link-write hit); vs ClockPro: CAR adapts ARC's recency/frequency
  balance rather than LIRS's.

## Uniform surface (LiteCache<K,V>)

- new LiteLru(capacity, options?) / new Sieve(capacity, options?) /
  new S3Fifo(capacity, options?) / new WTinyLfu(capacity, options?) /
  new Slru(capacity, options?) / new TwoQ(capacity, options?) /
  new Arc(capacity, options?) / new Lirs(capacity, options?) /
  new Lfu(capacity, options?) / new ClockPro(capacity, options?) /
  new LruK(capacity, options?) / new Mq(capacity, options?) /
  new Car(capacity, options?)
  - capacity: integer >= 1, else a [lite-lru]-tagged RangeError at the door.
- get(key) -> V | undefined. Applies the member's hit policy (LiteLru promotes to
  MRU; Sieve and S3Fifo set the visited bit; WTinyLfu bumps the frequency sketch
  and promotes within its segment).
- put(key, value, ttlMs?) -> void. Insert or update; at capacity evicts the
  member's victim first (firing onEvict). Amortized O(1) default / O(1) with
  keys:'int'. Optional positional ttlMs overrides the instance ttl default for this
  entry (positive ms, Infinity = never, omitted = default); see TTL below.
- has(key) -> boolean. Presence test; NEVER changes recency / visited state. A stale
  (TTL) entry is a MISS and is reaped in place.
- peek(key) -> V | undefined. Read without applying the hit policy. A stale (TTL)
  entry is a MISS and is reaped in place.
- delete(key) -> boolean. Remove; true if it was present.
- clear() -> void. Empty the cache; O(size) -- walks only the residents, never the
  capacity (S17 F7). The cold roster array may allocate (clear is not a hot path).
- purgeStale() -> number. Evict every currently-expired entry now (cold, O(size),
  fires onEvict per victim); returns the count. Returns 0 (NOT a throw) on a cache
  built without { ttl } -- it is a count, not a state (S17 S3), unlike stats(). (TTL)
- stats() -> CacheStats {hits,misses,evictions,puts}. Live per-instance counters,
  returned BY REFERENCE (borrowed -- copy what you keep). Requires { stats: true },
  else throws a [lite-lru] Error (fail-closed). (STATS)
- resetStats() -> void. Zero the four counters IN PLACE (a borrowed holder stays
  valid). Requires { stats: true }, else throws (fail-closed). (STATS)
- dump() -> CacheSnapshot. Serialize to a plain, structurally-cloneable snapshot
  (cold, MAY allocate <= 96 B/entry -- no zero-GC claim). Read-only (does not
  invalidate a live iterator). (SNAPSHOT)
- static Member.restore(snap, opts?) -> a FRESH instance. Backing/capacity/ttl-
  presence come FROM the snapshot; opts re-derives onEvict/clock/stats and supplies
  the ttl default when ttl is on. Fail closed on any mismatch. (SNAPSHOT)
- size -> number (0 .. capacity, getter). capacity -> number (getter).

## Construction options

- onEvict(key, value): called once per eviction with the evicted pair (e.g.
  return the value to a pool). Zero-GC: pass a hoisted function, not a per-ctor
  closure. REENTRANCY (decisions/0002): fires LAST, after the cache is fully
  consistent; it MUST NOT call put/get/delete/clear on the same instance (throws
  a [lite-lru]-tagged Error, fail-closed); has/peek ARE allowed inside it.
- keys: 'int' (decisions/0011): opt into an open-addressed typed-array keyed index
  for STRICT zero-alloc (even the index never allocates, no pre-fill caveat). Keys
  MUST be 32-bit signed integers [-2147483648, 2147483647]; a non-integer or
  out-of-range key throws a [lite-lru]-tagged TypeError. Values stay arbitrary.
  Omitted, the default is a JS Map: arbitrary keys, honestly AMORTIZED (its resize
  can allocate). An unknown keys value throws with a did-you-mean hint.
- keys: 'dense' + maxKey (decisions/0029): opt into a DIRECT-MAPPED, generation-stamped
  typed-array index for a SMALL, DENSE integer domain [0, maxKey]. The hot body is a
  single array read (NO hash, NO probe): `_gen[k] === _epoch ? _ixSlot[k] : NIL`. STRICT
  zero-alloc, and its index clear is an O(1) epoch bump (a disclosed-amortized O(U) reset
  only on epoch overflow past INT_MAX); clear() overall is O(size) -- it frees only the
  residents, never the maxKey domain (S17 F7). REQUIRES maxKey (an integer in [0, 2147483647], else a
  [lite-lru] TypeError); a key outside [0, maxKey] or non-integer throws (typeof guard
  FIRST; 0 is a LEGAL key). The honest co-headline is SPACE: O(maxKey), NOT O(entries).
  Use keys:'int' for large/sparse integer domains instead. DirectLru(cap, { maxKey }) is
  the convenience wrapper == new LiteLru(cap, { keys:'dense', maxKey }).
- ttl (decisions/0017): opt-in TTL default in ms. Positive-finite-or-Infinity, else
  a [lite-lru] RangeError. Allocates one fixed Float64Array expiry column (8 B/slot,
  never grown) ONLY when set; omitted keeps the ttl-OFF hot path byte-identical
  (_exp === null). Per-entry override via put(key, value, ttlMs).
- clock (decisions/0017; S17 S1/N4): injectable zero-arg fn returning ms. DEFAULT is
  performance.timeOrigin + performance.now() -- epoch-anchored, monotonic, zero-alloc
  (NOT Date.now, whose double return boxed on every TTL touch). Inject Date.now for
  wall-clock time. The library boxes NOTHING on the TTL path for ANY number clock
  (epoch-sized, fractional or logical -- backed by the N1 perf lanes). A non-function
  throws a [lite-lru] TypeError at the door; a clock returning a non-number (e.g. BigInt)
  or NaN fails closed (a tagged throw on put, read as stale/miss on get/has/peek), never
  "never expires". Only meaningful with ttl.
- stats: true (decisions/0019): opt into runtime counters (see STATS below). Any
  value other than true/omitted throws a [lite-lru] TypeError with a did-you-mean
  hint. Omitted keeps the stats-OFF hot path byte-identical (_stats === null).

## Stats (decisions/0019, D19)

- OPT-IN, zero-cost-when-off, pay-for-what-you-use. { stats: true } mints a fresh
  per-instance holder {hits,misses,evictions,puts}; omitted -> _stats === null and
  the hot path writes NOTHING (same writes-per-hit as the pre-stats build). All eight
  members, one LiteCache<K,V> surface.
- Counting law (D19.2): get -> hits (live resident) or misses (absent OR stale-TTL);
  put -> one puts always, plus one evictions when a new key is inserted at capacity;
  a stale-TTL get is a MISS AND an EVICTION (reaped in place). has/peek are hit/miss-
  NEUTRAL (inspections, not accesses); a stale has/peek still reaps = one eviction.
  Evictions are counted at exactly two sites: the capacity eviction in put, and _reap.
- Holder (D19.3): stats() returns the live holder BY REFERENCE (borrowed, like the
  iteration tuple) -- copy what you keep ({ ...cache.stats() }); resetStats() zeroes
  the SAME object in place. Holder identity is stable for the instance lifetime.
- Fields (D19.4): plain JS number fields (exact to 2^53), NOT an Int32Array (2^31
  wrap). Never overflows for a realistic cache.
- Fail closed (D19.5): stats()/resetStats() on a non-stats instance throw a
  [lite-lru] Error (null is not zero); the door rejects any non-true value.
- writesPerHit is NOT a runtime counter -- it stays a member-specific, gated,
  out-of-band MEASUREMENT (a runtime counter would need a store per hit).
- Gated: t6 Gate STATS (>= 60000 ops at capacity, { stats: true }) = 0 B/op, holder
  identity stable, holder plain with exactly the four names; Stats.test.js brute-tally
  parity over the T5 corpus (all thirteen members); t9 stats-double-count + stats-counts-
  peek controls (each diverges from the brute tally and fails).

## TTL (decisions/0017, D17)

- Opt-in, LAZY, pay-for-what-you-use. No timers, no async, no background sweep.
- An entry expires on the next get/has/peek that touches it: a stale touch is a MISS
  (no promotion / visited bump / sketch bump), reaped in place (fires onEvict via the
  0002 fire-after + reentrancy guard), returns undefined/false. purgeStale() is the
  optional eager path.
- Capacity eviction does NOT prefer stale slots: an untouched stale entry counts
  toward size until touched or purgeStale()'d.
- Fail-closed: ttlMs on a cache with no ttl configured throws [lite-lru]; ttl/ttlMs
  <= 0 / NaN throw [lite-lru] RangeError; Infinity = never (NEVER 0).
- All thirteen members support it identically over the shared SlotStore _exp column.
- Off-path decision (measured, D17): a single monomorphic this._exp===null guard.
  ttl-OFF writes-per-hit unchanged (LiteLru 0/5/4, Sieve/S3Fifo 0 links + 1 vis,
  WTinyLfu window-MRU 0); ttl-ON strict zero-alloc (maxMajor 0), _exp.byteLength
  stable under churn.
- vs lru-cache: lazy TTL only (no autopurge timer thread), no async fetch, no
  size-aware maxSize.

## Iteration (decisions/0018, D18)

- Every member is iterable: keys() -> IterableIterator<K>, values() ->
  IterableIterator<V>, entries() -> IterableIterator<[K,V]>, and [Symbol.iterator]
  === entries() (matches Map). Part of the uniform LiteCache<K,V> surface.
- Zero-GC per step: NO generators (a generator allocates an IteratorResult per
  yield). One hand-written iterator reuses a single {value,done} result mutated in
  place; the iterator object is allocated once per keys()/values()/entries() call
  (cold), never per step. Gated: >=10,000 next() steps at capacity = 0 B/op per step
  on all thirteen members. Honest pitch: our iterators allocate nothing per step,
  lru-cache's allocate. Never "lock-free".
- Per-member ORDER (only LiteLru is true recency): LiteLru MRU->LRU (recency);
  Sieve newest->oldest (FIFO insertion, NOT recency); S3Fifo MAIN newest->oldest
  THEN SMALL newest->oldest (ghost EXCLUDED, keys-only); WTinyLfu WINDOW THEN
  PROTECTED THEN PROBATION, each MRU->LRU (three segments concatenated); Lirs the
  LIR set THEN Q (resident HIR), each in list order -- RESIDENT ONLY, the
  non-resident history EXCLUDED.
- Borrowed-tuple caveat: entries()/[Symbol.iterator] yield ONE REUSED [k,v] array,
  mutated in place -- copy what you keep. Only a copying map materializes:
  Array.from(cache.entries(), ([k,v])=>[k,v]) or a manual per-step copy. A plain
  [...cache.entries()] / Array.from(cache) with NO map fn collects N references to the
  SAME reused tuple, which the completed walk then nulls (retention hardening,
  decisions/0018) -- so every element reads [undefined, undefined], NOT the data. Bare
  spread of entries is a bug; copy. keys()/values() yield the scalar directly, so
  [...cache.keys()] / [...cache.values()] materialize correctly (no aliasing hazard).
- Recency-neutral (like peek): a walk applies no promote / visited bump / sketch
  bump / segment relink, so it does not change the next eviction victim.
- TTL: iteration SKIPS stale entries (invisible) but does NOT reap them -- no
  structural mutation, so size is unchanged by a walk; use purgeStale() to reclaim.
- Fail closed: a structural mutation (put/delete/clear/evict/reap) mid-walk makes the
  next step throw a [lite-lru] Error (a single integer _ver on SlotStore, bumped only
  by mutations, NEVER on the get path -- so get writes-per-hit are unchanged:
  LiteLru 0/5/4, Sieve/S3Fifo 0 links + 1 vis, WTinyLfu window-MRU 0). A get()-induced
  reorder mid-walk is documented-unsupported (not caught).

## Snapshot / restore (decisions/0021, D21)

- Persist a warm cache and bring it back warm. dump() -> a plain, structurally-
  cloneable snapshot; Member.restore(snap, opts?) -> a FRESH instance. All eight
  members, one LiteCache<K,V> surface. COLD: no substrate field, no hot-path branch --
  a cache that never dumps is byte-identical to the pre-snapshot build.
- EXACT round-trip (D21.1/D21.4): a restored cache decides FUTURE evictions identically
  to the un-snapshotted twin fed the same trace. Slots are preserved verbatim, so every
  member captures ALL policy aux: Sieve's hand + visited bits; S3Fifo/TwoQ's keys-only
  ghost; W-TinyLFU's Count-Min sketch + aging counter; Arc's adaptive p + both ghosts.
  Lirs's stack-S order + per-slot LIR/inS bits + the bounded non-resident history.
  Dropping any of these is a fail-OPEN bug (t9 arc-p-dropped / sketch-dropped /
  ghost-omitted / lirs-drop-ins-bit / lirs-no-history each diverge).
- Plain graph (D21.1): plain arrays + plain numbers/values, NO typed-array views, so it
  round-trips through structuredClone (and JSON for JSON-safe keys/values). Object keys
  clone under structuredClone (new identity) -- documented, not a bug.
- Tag + fail-closed (D21.3 + decisions/0029): every snapshot carries { f:'litelru/1', m,
  cap, keys:'int'|'dense'|null, ttl:bool, t:captureMs, ... } (a dense snapshot also carries
  mk = maxKey so restore rebuilds the [0, mk] index). The backing is read from the store's
  explicit _kind tag, NOT duck-typed. restore() throws a [lite-lru] Error on a wrong/absent
  format tag, a member mismatch, a capacity/keys/ttl conflict vs opts, a dense snapshot with
  a missing/bad mk (or a non-dense snapshot that carries mk), a corrupt/short/missing field,
  and entries > cap (REJECT, never truncate -- capacity law 3). Restored size <= capacity
  always. null is not zero.
- opts (D21.2): backing/capacity/ttl-presence come FROM the snapshot; onEvict/clock/
  stats are RE-DERIVED from opts (a restored { stats: true } instance starts fresh-
  zeroed); the ttl DEFAULT is REQUIRED in opts when the snapshot has ttl on.
- TTL verbatim (D21.5, owner ruling): expiries are captured as ABSOLUTE ms deadlines,
  NOT rebased -- a restored entry expires exactly when it would have without the
  snapshot. The tag stamps capture time t so a future opt-in rebase is possible without
  a format bump (rebase is a non-goal this session).
- Cost (D21.6): dump budget <= 96 B/entry honest (measured 26.12 for LiteLru at cap
  4096; no zero-GC claim). A RESTORED cache's hot path is strict zero-alloc (0 B/op),
  backings never grow, writes-per-hit unchanged. dump() is read-only (no _ver bump), so
  a walk in progress is not invalidated.
- Gated: t6 Gate SNAP (0 B/op restored hot path + dump B/entry + writes-per-hit), t5
  round-trip differential over the 100k corpus (all thirteen members x both backings x ttl
  off/on), Snapshot.test.js (round-trip identity + 8 rejections + capacity law + interop
  + degenerate caps/keys/values), t7 4096 dump/restore cycles, t9 three drop controls.

## Invariants (suite CLAUDE.md + ROADMAP)

- Zero allocation on every hot path (get/put/delete/has/peek), for ALL members.
  The slot/list layer is STRICTLY zero-alloc; the keys:'int' index is strictly
  zero-alloc too; the default Map index is amortized (stated, not hidden).
- Fail closed: an invalid capacity throws (RangeError), an unknown keys value
  throws, a non-integer key in int mode throws (TypeError), a dense key outside
  [0, maxKey] or a missing/bad maxKey throws (TypeError). null is not zero.
- The D7 undefined-value contract: get/peek return undefined for EITHER "absent"
  OR "the stored value is literally undefined" -- indistinguishable via the return
  value; call has(key) to disambiguate. null is a normal, distinguishable value.
- Capacity is fixed and load-bearing: no member ever exceeds it, no growth path.
- Conservation invariant (validate(), test-only): size + freeListLength ===
  capacity; index.size === size; links reciprocal.
- Gated (torture): gc maxMajor 0, maxPauseMs 4, retained maxBytesPerCall 1,
  arrayBuffers growth 0; writes-per-hit LiteLru head/interior/tail 0/5/4 vs Sieve
  links/vis 0/1.

## Bench tool (Bench.mjs, decisions D20 / DEBATE item 13)

Ships in the tarball AND in exports as "./benchmark/Bench.mjs". A runnable ESM tool AND an
importable module; imports ONLY ./Lru.js (zero runtime deps).

- npm run bench  /  node benchmark/Bench.mjs  -> prints a per-workload, per-member table
    (columns: hit% / %OPT / wr/hit / ns/op / p95).
- import { runBench, beladyOpt } from '@zakkster/lite-lru/benchmark/Bench.mjs'
  - runBench(opts?) -> structured results (hitRatio, writesPerHit, nsPerOp,
    nsPerOpMedian, nsPerOpP95, pctOptimal) per workload (zipf / loop / scan; or a
    caller-supplied trace) per member, plus each workload's OPT. Deterministic for a
    given seed. ns/op is wall-clock and MACHINE-LOCAL; hit ratio is a deterministic
    OUTPUT of the named trace, never a headline or cross-library claim.
    KNOBS (all optional, all echoed in a top-level `tuning` object -- config stays
    exactly {capacity,length,seed}): `alphas` (zipf exponent sweep, default [1.0]);
    `keyspaceRatio` (keyspace = capacity*ratio, default 16, was hardcoded *16);
    `repeats` (timed passes per member, default 5). With defaults the set is exactly
    ['zipf','loop','scan'] with byte-identical traces; any other `alphas` names each
    workload 'zipf-a<A>' (e.g. runBench({ alphas: ZIPF_ALPHAS }) -> zipf-a0.7 /
    zipf-a0.9 / zipf-a1.0 / zipf-a1.2). ns/op TIMING: each member now runs one warmup
    + `repeats` timed passes; nsPerOp === nsPerOpMedian (median, back-compat) and
    nsPerOpP95 is the nearest-rank 95th percentile -- variance you can see, not a
    single throughput headline.
  - ZIPF_ALPHAS = [0.7, 0.9, 1.0, 1.2] -- the opt-in skew-sweep constant.
  - beladyOpt(trace, capacity) -> { hits, misses, hitRate }. Belady's clairvoyant
    offline optimum (evict the resident whose NEXT use is farthest). A REFERENCE
    ORACLE, NEVER a production policy; differential-tested vs a brute-force O(N*C)
    OPT in the torture gate (t8). SCALE CEILING: beladyOpt allocates an Int32Array(n)
    next-use table + a Map over the whole trace, so OPT (not the caches) caps a
    "scale" run -- fine at ~5M ops, heavy toward ~50M.
  - webTrace(opts) -> a seeded, deterministic "web-like" trace: a diurnal hot set
    that slowly ROTATES across the keyspace (period) interleaved with a zipf tail
    (hotFraction / exponent). Exported; NOT in the default set.
  - parseIntTrace(text, opts?) -> integer Array from columnar/CSV text (delimiter,
    column, comment prefix, skipHeader). Takes a STRING, not a path (no node:fs);
    throws a [lite-lru]-tagged RangeError on a non-integer token. Feed the result to
    runBench({ workloads }) to replay your own captured trace.

## Tree-shaking (ROADMAP law 7, decisions/0012)

Single PascalCase Lru.js with named exports + sideEffects:false: import { Sieve }
drops LiteLru's body from the bundle (and vice versa). The shared substrate is
INTERNAL, not an export; there is NO subpath-per-policy. Bench.mjs is a separate
runnable tool, not a second implementation.

## Demo (decisions/0022, D22; dev-only, NEVER shipped)

demo/ animates ONE shared trace through all thirteen members, each panel drawn STRICTLY from that member's live dump() snapshot (D22.1, no shadow state), with a running %-of-Belady-optimal line. npm run demo (headless per-member summary via demo/Visualize.mjs) and npm run demo:serve (zero-dep Node server demo/serve.mjs -> http://localhost:8013/, browser page demo/visuals.html imports only ../Lru.js). demo/ is absent from files[]; Lru.js / Lru.d.ts / Bench.mjs are consumed, never edited. Must be run through the Node server (npm run demo:serve -> http://localhost:8013/), NOT as a static file or an IDE static preview: /trace.json is a dynamic route and ES modules need an http origin, so off-server the page fails closed with an actionable message instead of hanging.

## API (1.19.0)

Named exports from @zakkster/lite-lru:

- LiteLru: the classic LRU member (also the default export).
- DirectLru: LiteLru pinned to the keys:'dense' direct-mapped backing (decisions/0029); new DirectLru(cap, { maxKey }) == new LiteLru(cap, { keys:'dense', maxKey }), zero policy duplication.
- Sieve: the SIEVE member.
- S3Fifo: the S3-FIFO member.
- WTinyLfu: the W-TinyLFU member.
- Slru: the Segmented-LRU member.
- TwoQ: the full-2Q member.
- Arc: the Adaptive Replacement Cache member.
- Lirs: the LIRS member (recency-of-recency; scan/loop-resistant; bounded non-resident history).
- Lfu: the O(1) EXACT Least-Frequently-Used member (frequency buckets; LRU tie-break; the exact counterpart to WTinyLfu's approximate sketch).
- ClockPro: the CLOCK-Pro member (CLOCK approximation of LIRS; recency-of-recency on a clock with a 0-link-write hit + a self-tuning hot/cold split; bounded non-resident history).
- LruK: the LRU-K (K=2) member (the original recency-of-recency policy; evicts by the K-th backward distance; warm hit 0 links + 2 stamps, cold->warm promotion at most 5 (2..5) links, non-exceedable; bounded keys-only history).
- Mq: the Multi-Queue (m=8) member (frequency bands + logical-time decay; a hit is real band-relink surgery (0, or at most 5 (4..5), links) + a fixed 7-step aging sweep, a PROVEN non-exceedable <=33 links + 3 stamps per access, NOT a 0-write hit; evicts the lowest-queue tail; bounded keys-only + refcount Qout).
- Car: the CAR (Clock with Adaptive Replacement) member (the CLOCK reformulation of ARC; T1/T2 clocks + B1/B2 ghosts + one adaptive p, no knobs; a hit is 0 links + exactly 1 _st reference-bit store like Sieve/ClockPro; miss+evict amortized O(1) / worst-case O(capacity), NO pinned constant bound; evicts the first unreferenced clock page).
- VERSION: '1.19.0'

Named exports from @zakkster/lite-lru/benchmark/Bench.mjs:

- runBench(opts?), beladyOpt(trace, capacity), backingCompare(opts?), ZIPF_ALPHAS,
  plus the seeded trace generators (zipfTrace, loopTrace, scanTrace, webTrace,
  makePrng) and the parseIntTrace(text, opts?) columnar loader, used to build or
  replay reproducible traces.

## Testing

- npm test        -- 2359 node:test cases (all thirteen members, recency/SIEVE/S3-FIFO/
  W-TinyLFU/Slru/TwoQ/Arc/LIRS/LFU/ClockPro/LRU-K/Multi-Queue/CAR laws, TTL laws + fail-closed + purgeStale, stats parity,
  iteration order, snapshot/restore round-trip + fail-closed, degenerate keys/values
  + degenerate caps 1..4, dts drift, family surface).
- npm run test:types -- tsc: the LiteCache<K,V> surface + the one-line-swap check.
- npm run torture -- @zakkster/lite-leak + lite-gc-profiler, --expose-gc: prints
  "ok"; tiers t0/t1/t2/t5/t6/t7/t8/t9 (t8 = the Belady OPT gate).
- npm run torture:controls -- the deliberately-broken variants; every gate fails.
- npm run test:perf -- @zakkster/lite-perf-gate (dev-only devDep; ships NOTHING to the
  tarball), a node:test-native HARD zero-alloc gate that COMPLEMENTS torture t6. 26
  scenarios (get-hit + put-churn per member) on the keys:'int' backing, proving 0
  scavenges across N=200000 and k*N=1.6M, with old-gen / arrayBuffers / the int-index
  `grows` counter all pinned to 0, plus a mustFail object-key churn that MUST trip the
  gate (teeth every run). The HARD gate covers ONLY keys:'int' (strict zero-alloc,
  decisions/0011); the Map-backing hot paths are AMORTIZED (resize may scavenge) and are
  covered by t6, NOT here. Retained-heap keeps the tool default 64 KB (heapUsed deltas
  are noisy); the proof is the scavenge / old-gen / external / counter lanes at strict 0.
- npm run bench   -- the measurement tool (repo + shipped).
- npm run verify  -- test + test:types + torture + controls + test:perf, the publish gate.

## Composability

- Measure with Bench.mjs / beladyOpt on your trace, then deploy the winning
  member behind the SAME LiteCache surface -- the measured policy IS the shipped
  policy, by construction.
- @zakkster/lite-signal: zero-GC reactive graph for hot paths.
- @zakkster/lite-binary-reader: zero-GC reader for raw / foreign binary buffers.
